provisions.title: Implementation
provisions.body:
The document has been created and approved by the General Assembly of 29.11.2025.
The document and its rules will be implemented from the 2029 season (01/01/2029).
Competitors will have 3 seasons to align their equipment with this document and its rules.

provisions.title: Definition
provisions.body:
Bascinets with perforated visors are helmets with movable perforated visors. Such visors do not include Eye slots.
This type of visor is depicted in some rare manuscripts in Western Europe from the late 14th century and early 15th century. A handful of later designs showing this kind of visor still survive through the 15th century.
There is no consensus among armor experts where such manuscripts depict actual perforated visors or badly drawn regular helmets (hundskulls for example).
Those helmets use a solid metal visor to protect the face, attached by 2 different system:

● Attached on the forehead by a movable piece of metal, similar to the “spoon” from Klappvisor,

● Attached to the dome with hinges at the temples, similar to Pivoting visored Bascinets.

Spoon

provisions.title: Bascinets with perforated and forehead attached visor
provisions.body:
The term “Bascinets with perforated and forehead attached visor” will be abbreviated to “Perforated Klappvisor Bascinets’ for the remainder of the document.

Perforated Klappvisor Bascinets can be seen in a couple of manuscripts, from 1389 to 1420/1430.

Perforated Klappvisor Bascinets can have a visor with a rounded profile or a sharp profile. The shape of the profile does not change the approved and denied time periods.

Perforated Klappvisor Bascinets are Approved for Transitional armors.
Perforated Klappvisor Bascinets are Denied for 14th century armors.

Perforated Klappvisor Bascinets can be Approved for 15th century armors with a coherent project.
We strongly recommend sending an email to authenticity@buhurtinternational.com before placing an order for such armor.

Vindobonensis 2762, Wenzel Bible - 1389 - Austria Pal.lat.1888 - 1430 - Germany

Géttinger MS Philos. 63 Bellifortis - 1405 - Germany

provisions.title: Bascinets with perforated side-hinged attached visor
provisions.body:
The term “Bascinets with perforated side-hinged attached visor” will be abbreviated to “Side-hinged Perforated Bascinets’” for the remainder of the document.

Side-hinged Perforated Bascinets must have a visor with a rounded profile Side-hinged Perforated Bascinets are Approved for Transitional armors.

Side-hinged Perforated Bascinets are Denied for 14th century and 15th century armors.

Vindobonensis 2762, Wenzel Bible - 1389 - Austria

Wenceslas Bible - 1390/1400 - Germany

provisions.title: Great Bascinets with perforated visor
provisions.body:
Later during the 15th-century, a handful of contemporary designs show the use of perforated visors, despite a great lack of representation in art.

Great Bascinets with perforated visors must have a visor with a rounded profile.
Great Bascinets with perforated visors are Approved for 15th century armors.

Great Bascinets with perforated visors are Denied for 14th century and Transitional armors.

German Great Bascinet, MET

Grand Bacinet private collection - 1450/1475- southern Germany or Austria

provisions.title: Bicoques with perforated visor
provisions.body:
Later during the 15th century, a handful of contemporary designs show the use of perforated visor, despite a great lack of representation in art.

Bicoques with perforated visors must have a visor with a rounded profile.
Bicoques with perforated visors Approved for 15th century armors.

Bicoques with perforated visors are Denied for 14th century and Transitional armors.

provisions.title: General Requirements
provisions.body:
Reproductions must closely resemble the appearance and proportions of either bascinets, great bascinets or bicoque respective sources.

Any metal part of the helmet must conform to the “Armors and Weapons Aesthetics and Decorations document.

Any textile or leather part of the helmet must conform to the “Textiles and Leather” document.

provisions.title: Visor
provisions.body:
The visor must not be too long or too short, it must respect the proportions of historical sources.

It is allowed to add a metal plate to protect the throat. Such a plate must be strong enough to endure full contact fight and must be concealed under the aventail.

A leather strap can be used to secure the visor down.
It is permitted to weld the visor down. Welded visors must resemble a functional removable visor.
The hinge must be reproduced as per historical sources.

Breath holes should be round and must not exceed a diameter of 10mm. Breath holes must not be so numerous that they compromise the helm’s structural integrity. It is acceptable to mirror breath holes to both sides.

Breath holes of another shape must be documented by historical sources to be allowed.

Profile of visors:

● Sharp-profile visors Visors with a sharp profile must clearly present a pointy profile.

● Rounded-profile visors Visors with a rounded profile must clearly present a globose profile.

provisions.title: Aventails
provisions.body:
Bascinets with perforated visors must be worn with chainmail aventails, fabric aventails, or scales aventails.

Great Bascinets and Bicoques can not be worn with chainmail aventails, fabric aventails or scales aventails.

Aventails must conform to the “Aventails” document.

Aventails must be attached to the bascinet by a system of leather and vervelles.

The aventail must be fastened down to the edge of a padded pelerine attached to the helmet liner.
Any additional protective plates covering the cervical spine must be hidden under the aventail.

provisions.title: Others
provisions.body:
All helmets with perforated visors may be decorated in the spirit of medieval styles, such as orle, torse, decorated aventails (with copper/brass chainmail rings), vervelle covers and coat of arms badges etc.

Such decoration must be made in coherence with historical sources.
Using modern and/or offensive imagery and slogans is prohibited.
